newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Tung loses ground in opinion polls.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tung loses ground in opinion polls.

text.p: A decision by Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa to put a property tycoon in charge of housing policy has dented his popularity, a Hong Kong newspaper poll published on Tuesday showed.
A telephone poll conducted by the Ming Pao on Monday asked 565 people to rate Tung's ability and credibility on a scale of one to nine, with nine the top mark.

Tung, who will step into Governor Chris Patten's shoes when the British colony reverts to China on July 1, scored 4.88 points for ability, a drop of more than one point since a similar survey on February 24.
He scored 4.85 points for credibility, down from 5.7 points last month.
The independent Chinese-language paper attributed the decline to Tung's appointment of property surveyor and real estate consultant Leung Chun-ying as head of a committee to map out housing strategy.
Politicians, both from the pro-democracy camp and the pro-Beijing big business lobby, have denounced Leung's appointment as a potential conflict of interest.
Critics have complained on radio talk shows and in newspaper correspondence columns, traditional outlets for public dissatisfaction. A small group of demonstrators picketed his office on Monday.
Housing is a sensitive issue in tiny, crowded Hong Kong where costs are among the highest in the world and have made owning a home a pipe dream for many young families.
"Clearly, there is a conflict of interest for Leung Chun-ying to formulate Hong Kong's long-term housing policy," the Hong Kong Economic Times said on Tuesday.

With 98 days to go until Hong Kong is handed over to China, Tung is facing his first real test of handling public opinion since being anointed leader-in-waiting by a committee vetted by Beijing in December.
Tung's decision last week to allocate "portfolios" to members of his Executive Council, or inner cabinet of advisers, broke with tradition and ruffled some feathers.
Previous governors picked their Executive Council members from all walks of life to tap a range of expertise but did not hand out specific responsibilities.

Tung, an experienced business tycoon but political novice, has been racing against the clock to form an administration and come to terms with the world of politics in preparation for taking on Patten's mantle.
